source: NASA/JPL and USGS Mars landing-site coordinates (planetocentric, east-positive); mission dates from NASA, CNSA and ESA press material

sites.name: Mars 3
sites.blurb: The first soft landing on Mars. It transmitted for about twenty seconds, then fell silent in a global dust storm.

sites.name: Viking 1
sites.blurb: The first successful Mars lander worked for six years and sent the first photographs from the surface.

sites.name: Viking 2
sites.blurb: Photographed frost on the ground at 48° north and ran the same life-detection experiments as its twin.

sites.name: Mars Pathfinder
sites.blurb: Bounced down on airbags and released Sojourner, a rover the size of a microwave, the first wheels on Mars.

sites.name: Spirit
sites.blurb: Planned for 90 days, drove 7.7 km over six years and found silica deposits from ancient hot springs.

sites.name: Opportunity
sites.blurb: Drove 45 km in 14 years, the longest drive on another world, and found hematite that formed in water.

sites.name: Phoenix
sites.blurb: Dug into the arctic plains and confirmed water ice a few centimetres below the surface.

sites.name: Curiosity
sites.blurb: Lowered by a rocket-powered sky crane. Still climbing Mount Sharp, reading billions of years of lake sediments.

sites.name: InSight
sites.blurb: Listened to marsquakes for four years and measured the size of the planet's liquid core.

sites.name: Perseverance
sites.blurb: Caching rock samples in an ancient river delta for return to Earth. Carried Ingenuity, the first aircraft to fly on another planet.

sites.name: Zhurong (Tianwen-1)
sites.blurb: China's first Mars rover drove 1.9 km and found signs of water activity younger than expected.
